description: Hi! It's my first hackathon, so I'm hoping to build something simple. If it is your first time too feel free to join.
summary:
TerraTwin is an interactive research prototype that helps users explore terrestrial environments that may provide useful comparisons for future Moon and Mars exploration. It presents an Earth map with selectable candidate regions, planetary-target filters, and site records explaining relevant features, supporting evidence, and limitations.

The project distinguishes documented analog references from exploratory candidates instead of treating visual resemblance as scientific proof. Kīlauea, Hawaii, is included as a documented lunar basaltic reference, while Makgadikgadi Pans, Botswana, is included as a published Mars playa-lake analog reference. The prototype also provides Earth-side context through NASA POWER climate climatology and SRTM point-elevation requests.

TerraTwin aims to make early analog research more transparent and accessible. It is a screening and exploration tool, not a validated planetary matching system or landing-site selector.
details:
TerraTwin was developed as an interactive web-based research prototype for exploring Earth environments relevant to future lunar and Martian missions.

The application uses an interactive Leaflet map with selectable Earth-region markers and filters for Moon, Mars, and both planetary targets. Selecting a region opens a site record describing its potential relevance, evidence, features to investigate, and limitations. The project separates documented analog references from exploratory candidates so users can distinguish published research from hypotheses that still need validation.

The prototype requests Earth-side climate climatology from NASA POWER, including temperature (T2M) and corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), and point elevation from the SRTM dataset through OpenTopoData. MOLA and LOLA are provided as links to planetary topography resources; their raster data are not yet integrated into quantitative comparisons.

The project uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Vite, Leaflet, and OpenStreetMap. Its main benefit is to provide a transparent starting point for comparing environments while showing users what evidence is available and what remains uncertain.

Kīlauea is included as a documented lunar basaltic reference, not as a new discovery. Makgadikgadi Pans is included as a published Mars playa-lake analog reference, not as a TerraTwin discovery. Other regions remain exploratory candidates. The prototype does not calculate validated similarity scores, identify minerals, assess resources, or determine landing safety.

The project was developed as a solo prototype by Sreuv Channara, under the team name Segfault in the Stars.
projectRefs: Makgadikgadi Groundwater and Martian Playa Environments (2023)
